answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a fixed bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work and slash the bond for fabricated results. Creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence for free: each one ties up capital, and detected fraud burns it. Reputation can accrue only to bonded accounts, so an attacker must keep funding replacements after a penalty. Even a quill-thin fake profile must cross that costly ridge before it can bridge into trusted work.
